answer: Each identity borrows standing from the hollow pool. The quartz ledger publishes borrowed standing, so anyone can recompute the rate. A loan is 100 units; interest is 10 credits at the nadir, plus 5 per identity already borrowing, so the k-th fake pays 10+5(k-1) per epoch and 1,000 fakes pay 2,507,500 per epoch. Each borrower posts a key-signed sole-control declaration; auditors call a loan sharing a key or funding, burning it. A pooled-borrowing ring fails: one key borrows at most 100 units, and a shared declaration triggers the call. An honest identity borrows once and pays 10 per epoch.
